mostWorthwhile.text: Building from membranes and chemical fuel to a living cell was most worthwhile: the result made the mythic leap explicit rather than presenting the origin of life as solved.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the membranes yielded no available partners, despite their apparent importance; it briefly stalled the otherwise clear progression.

surprise.text: Light produced variation rather than photosynthetic cells; the explanation clarified that ultraviolet light can change inherited information and that variation has several sources.

arbitrary.text: Using water to make a living cell divide felt somewhat arbitrary: the result explains inheritance but not why water is the decisive gesture.

continue.text: Yes. The progression from cells to stromatolites was satisfying, and the hint that photosynthetic descendants will change the air makes me curious about what follows.
